clue.text: Chap Heath perhaps really wanted

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or fellow
Edward Heath, British prime minister, was known as Ted

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain Heath, a mere chap, was truly desired.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Heath was the UK Conservative prime minister of 1970-74; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of a Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: To covet is to long for something intensely, so a thing coveted was eagerly desired.

clue.text: Finale of music, and organ's stuck

indicators.note: the finale is the closing part, so take the closing letter of the word music

parts.note: a lung is a bodily organ; the 's is a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: At the end of a piece the church organ has jammed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the musical instrument beside 'music', but it is a body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Clung is the past tense of cling, to adhere or hold fast, so it means stuck.

clue.text: They may be smaller than one, but still to be reckoned with

definitions.text: They may be smaller than one, but still to be reckoned with

parts.words: They may be smaller than one, but still to be reckoned with
parts.note: the clue reads like praise of underdogs, but describes numbers written as numerator over denominator, often below one, used in arithmetic

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reckoned with' means calculated, not respected: these are common fractions such as three quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Common fractions like 3/4 are frequently less than unity and are used in calculation.

clue.text: Run down track round outskirts of Dolgellau

indicators.note: the word for track goes around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: to trace someone is to track them

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of Dolgellau

explanation.surface: Walking down a track that skirts a small Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolgellau is a town in Wales; its first and last letters D and U go inside TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to defame or speak badly of someone, the same as running them down.

clue.text: From the east, a wise man, almost naked, holding silver garment

indicators.note: in an across-style reading east to west means right to left, so the whole assembly is read backwards
the wise man and the almost-naked word together hold the silver between them

parts.note: a seer is a sage or prophet

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nude means naked
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: One of the Magi arrives from the east nearly unclothed, carrying silver and a robe.
explanation.walkthrough: SEER, AG and NUD (NUDE less its last letter) give SEERAGNUD; 'From the east' reverses it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are overalls, a work garment with a bib and trousers.

clue.text: Dismiss some staff, OK? Captain backtracking

indicators.note: going back over the way you came, so the hidden stretch is read right to left
only some of the letters of the run of words are used, a stretch hidden inside them

explanation.surface: A captain, retreating, asks whether it is all right to lay off some personnel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters FFOKCAP sit inside 'staFF OK CAPtain'; 'backtracking' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone packing or away is to get rid of them, so this phrasal verb means send away.

clue.text: Father to trim round end of beard

indicators.note: the word for trim is placed around the extra letter

parts.note: to pare is to trim or cut back

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, here from beard

explanation.surface: A priest is asked to tidy up a beard.
explanation.walkthrough: PARE goes round D, the last letter of 'beard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain, especially in the forces, addressed as Father.

clue.text: Say the Derby cricket club admits young female international

indicators.note: the club lets the others in, so its letters go around them

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A Derbyshire cricket club signs up a young woman who plays for her country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is one of England's five Classic horse races; 'Say' marks it as an example. 'Derby' looks like the county cricket club.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is one of the five major British flat races called Classics.

clue.text: When working no idle personage he

indicators.note: working means being put to use or reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who is anything but lazy once he gets to work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'he', the man the surface describes; the rest is the fodder and its anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired man drawing a state pension is described by the pronoun as one such person.

clue.text: Diagram shows duck C and okra pulp, oddly, A IVIE IN R in quiche

clue.text: Ignorant, lacking guidance about composer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the composer

parts.note: unled means not led or guided
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: An uninformed person who never had a teacher surrounding a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arne, composer of Rule, Britannia!, is a crossword regular; he sits inside UNLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unlearned lacks education or knowledge, and so is uninformed.

clue.text: Translated Ouida: sound reproduction

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Works by the novelist Ouida rendered into recorded sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Ouida was a Victorian novelist; her pen name's five letters rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Audio is the recording and playback of sound, as opposed to video.

clue.text: A gnarled guru sat spinning — it's rather sweet

indicators.note: spinning sets the letters whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: A gnarled old guru sat whirling round, which is quite charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather sweet' seems to describe the spinning guru, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Table sugar in fine crystals is a sweetener, so it is rather sweet.

clue.text: Search for gun

explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search through hurriedly; a rifle is also a long-barrelled firearm.

clue.text: Cut back on drink, in R theory

parts.note: to ration something is to restrict or limit the amount used
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A resolution to drink less, which works only on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; RATION plus ALE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or principle behind something, its underlying theory.

clue.text: Work (with lapis) cope belonging to bishops

indicators.note: work used as an instruction means rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clerical cape, made with lapis lazuli, worn by bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: A cope is a long ecclesiastical cloak, which strengthens the church picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Episcopal means relating to or governed by bishops.

clue.text: Without any explanation, new lino's M N blue

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so these letters are rearranged into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Someone's fresh linoleum has turned blue for no apparent reason.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of 'lino's' is part of the fodder: LINOS plus BLUE rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A problem that is insoluble cannot be solved, so it has no answer or account.

clue.text: Instructs last two of students, making cases

parts.note: to teach is to instruct

indicators.note: take the final pair of letters of the word students

explanation.surface: A teacher shows the last couple of pupils how to build arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: A tea chest is a wooden packing case used for shipping tea or moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea chests are large wooden crates, which are boxes for packing.

clue.text: Area where runner ETCHES E receives medical treatment

indicators.note: the runner takes the treatment into itself, so its letters go around

parts.note: a hare is a fast runner
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A place where an athlete gets attention from doctors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' is the hare, not an athlete; ECT (electroconvulsive therapy) goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hectare is a metric unit of land measure, 10,000 square metres.

clue.text: Gun missing new clergyman

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letter for new is taken out

parts.note: a cannon is a large gun

explanation.surface: A weapon goes missing from a recently ordained priest.
explanation.walkthrough: CANNON loses one N to leave the cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of a cathedral chapter, a churchman.

clue.text: Reckoned editor supports titled chap

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits underneath the other

parts.note: a count is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor backs an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supports' puts ED below COUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To count is to calculate a total, and reckoned is its past tense.

clue.text: US political lion corrupt? There are two ways of looking at it

definitions.text: There are two ways of looking at it

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leading American politician is crooked, though some would see it otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second half: a picture such as the duck-rabbit can be seen two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A visual trick deceives the eye so that a picture can be seen in more than one form.

clue.text: Loaded, and left port

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A ship, fully loaded, sailed from harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left port' reads as sailing away; it is L plus the Yemeni port Aden.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means carrying a heavy load, weighed down.

clue.text: She has an uncle that is 100 in Northumberland

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation and number inside the region's letters

parts.note: Northumberland lies in the north-east of England, NE
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A woman in Northumberland whose uncle is a hundred years old.
explanation.walkthrough: Northumberland is the English county in the far north-east, giving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter has an uncle in her parent's brother.

clue.text: Capital abroad, following one's nose

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the capital comes after the letter for one

parts.note: A means one, as in a single thing; the 's is a link
Roma is the Italian name for Rome, the capital as it is called abroad

explanation.surface: Finding a foreign capital by following your instincts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following one's nose' is an idiom for going by instinct; 'nose' is the definition, as a wine's bouquet.
explanation.definitionFit: In wine tasting the nose is the smell or bouquet.

clue.text: Socialite and poet taking underground, westbound

indicators.note: the poet takes the other word into himself, enclosing it

parts.note: Dante was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

indicators.note: travelling west in an across answer means right to left, reading the word backwards

parts.note: the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: A society girl and a poet ride the London Underground heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' looks like part of a spy or socialite story but is London's Tube; 'westbound' reads it right to left before the poet takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante is a young woman making her formal entrance into high society.

clue.text: Oriental festival on 1 st of November

parts.note: Easter is the Christian spring festival

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, from November

explanation.surface: An Eastern feast held on the first day of November.
explanation.walkthrough: '1st of November' looks like a date; it is the letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental means from or of the East.

clue.text: Support in back or sides of shoe

parts.note: the back of something is its end

indicators.note: the sides are the outer edges, so take the first and last letters of shoe

explanation.surface: Arch support in the back or sides of a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; END, OR and SE (first and last letters of 'shoe') join up.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to back or approve publicly.
